item.title: New Federal Report Shows RTO Backfires on Federal Talent
item.description: A recent GAO report found that limiting telework at SSA led to recruiting challenges.

item.title: Schedule F and Draining the Swamp: ~50,000 Federal Jobs May Lose Civil-Service Appeal Rights
item.description: OPM issued a final Schedule F rule, stripping civil-service appeals from ~50K federal employees to ease firing and reduce efforts to derail policy initiatives.

item.title: Retirement Surge Pushes OPM Retirement Backlog Over 54k in January
item.description: The OPM retirement backlog topped 54,000 in January, but digital processing is improving efficiency.

item.title: Reinstated Reporting Shows Official Time Costs Rose 54% Over Five Years
item.description: OPM has resumed publishing official time reports, and the new data show that costs have risen sharply over a five-year period.

item.title: Should Federal Employees Invest in Gold?
item.description: Gold's performance has been making headlines recently, but does that make it a good investment for federal employees?

item.title: Challenging Channeling: Does CSRA Dysfunction Vest District Courts With Jurisdiction?
item.description: Federal employee lawsuits challenge the Trump administration directly in court outside established CSRA channels. Will this tactic succeed?

item.title: I’m Retiring Soon… Do I Have Enough in My TSP?
item.description: Federal employees can assess retirement readiness by combining fixed income with safe TSP withdrawals. These are some strategies.

item.title: Can OPM Revoke MSPB’s Authority to Hear RIF Appeals?
item.description: RIF appeal rights to the MSPB are not statutory—they exist only because of OPM regulation. A new proposed rule would return RIF appeals to OPM.

item.title: Bad Bosses Get Lied to More
item.description: Research shows employees lie to avoid bad bosses. Learn why this happens and tips on how to prevent it.

item.title: Federal Employees Could See 4.1% Pay Raise in 2027 Under New Bill
item.description: The 2027 federal pay raise debate has begun. New legislation proposes a 4.1% raise for the federal workforce next year.
